questions.key_step: Coefficients of x^2 and x^3 give two linear equations in a,b.
questions.justification: Two linear equations from two coefficients, routine chain of standard steps; below 2025-P2-Q10 (L4) which needs the largest-coefficient analysis.

questions.key_step: nCr=nC23 gives two cases; combine with 2n-5r=1.
questions.justification: Single general-term step with a two-case coefficient condition; routine, option-based.

questions.key_step: (1-x)(1+x+x^2)=1-x^3 collapses the product.
questions.justification: One familiar pairing trick (1-x)(1+x+x^2)=1-x^3 then a single coefficient; like 2026-P2-Q4 (L1) in idea but with two short stages.

questions.key_step: r*nCr=n*(n-1)C(r-1) twice (or E[X^2]).
questions.justification: Absorption identity applied twice (or E[X^2]); chain of standard binomial-sum steps.

questions.key_step: Match exponents of the two parts with the sixth power.
questions.justification: Two-part product, general-term exponent matching; routine multi-step.

questions.key_step: G.P. sum factorises with 49^63+1; maximality via order.
questions.justification: G.P. sum and factorisation difference of powers; maximality is a mild extra idea but options guide.

questions.key_step: Ratio of nCr gives r=6k^2-19; bound r.
questions.justification: Ratio of binomial coefficients then a bounded integer count; routine with small care on range.

questions.key_step: Even powers of the surd survive: 2T6(x).
questions.justification: Even-power surd expansion and a short polynomial expansion; routine.

questions.key_step: x-free term 16C8*2^8/sin^8(2theta); extreme at end points.
questions.justification: General term plus the range of sin2θ on two intervals; a few standard steps.

questions.key_step: Differentiate (1+x)^15 at x=-1; odd-index sum 2^13.
questions.justification: Two ideas linked: differentiate and set x=-1, then odd-index sum with a leftover last term; like 2023-P1-Q13 (L4) in topic but far lighter.

questions.key_step: Hockey stick, or recognise sum of squares.
questions.justification: Hockey stick or sum of squares; short standard chain.

questions.key_step: Middle term 10C5 x sqrt(1-x); maximise.
questions.justification: Two ideas: middle term, then single-variable maximisation (calculus or AM-GM); two stages.

questions.key_step: f(1), f(-1) give even/odd coefficient sums.
questions.justification: Even/odd coefficient sums via f(1), f(-1); one familiar move plus reading the floor limits, a little above L1.

questions.key_step: Reverse and add: 2S=30*60C30.
questions.justification: Reverse-and-add trick with the sum of squares of binomial coefficients; standard.

questions.key_step: Ratio (11-r)/r simplifies to r(11-r)^2; power sums.
questions.justification: Ratio of consecutive coefficients then power sums; routine arithmetic chain.

questions.key_step: K=2^98, middle term, ratio 100/101.
questions.justification: Several stages (odd-coefficient sum, middle term, ratio, 2-adic form) each simple; no options to hide a slip in the factor 100/101.

questions.key_step: G.P. with ratio x/(1+x); sum (1+x)^501-x^501.
questions.justification: G.P. of binomial terms collapses to a closed form; one standard idea.

questions.key_step: Conjugate (8sqrt3-13)^13 in (0,1); parity of x-x'.
questions.justification: Conjugate-power/fractional-part idea on two radicals, needing the (0,1) check for each; familiar to Main students but two stages.

questions.key_step: Odd-index binomial sum 2^50 over 51!.
questions.justification: One move: reciprocal factorial pairs become binomial coefficients, sum 2^50; like 2024-P2-Q3 (L1).

questions.key_step: Numerator 2n(2n-1)+8n+8 splits into three exponential series.
questions.justification: Three-part decomposition of the numerator into exponential series; chain of standard steps.
